doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Growing up in Roxbury; building four-wheel carts
summary: Roxbury was a mixed street; his childhood hobby was building carts numbered 13.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: What neighborhood did you grow up in?
Roxbury, Massachusetts, which at that time, the street that we lived on was like the U.N. We had a little of everything there, all kind of people, which was great.
So you basically grew up in an integrated neighborhood and had a variety of friends?
Do you remember any things that you used to do as a child, any childhood games?
Definitely. I used to like to build carts, four-wheel carts. That was my hobby, nails and hammers, building and driving the fast carts, with number 13 on them, which was my birthday.
I don’t know about that, but that’s when I was born. My mother often says it was her lucky number.
